_description: Every measurable claim security-mcp's docs make about itself, with a probe or test that proves or disproves it. Run `node scripts/verify-claims.mjs --strict`. status TRUE means the claim is currently verified true; SCOPED means the doc was rewritten to what is actually true and the registry records the walk-back (rewrite.reason explains why).

claims.verbatim: 900 fix templates covering 100% (900/900) of detection IDs
claims.note: First run of this claim (2026-07-17) found the sets were NOT equal despite equal counts: EVAL_UNAVAILABLE_THREAT_INTEL (a live rule, added in the Wave-1 evaluability fix) had no template, and DEP_UNPINNED_VERSION (a template) had no live rule pointing to it — a dangling remnant of a renamed check. Fixed both in src/gate/remediation-map.ts so the claim is now literally true, not just count-coincidentally true.

claims.verbatim: every shipped skill is registered in skills-manifest.json with a sha256 that matches its current SKILL.md content
claims.note: Verifies two things per skill, bulk (91 skills, one claim — see the note in scripts/verify-claims.mjs on why this replaced 91 near-duplicate per-skill entries): (1) skills-manifest.json's key set equals the set of skills/*/SKILL.md directories (excluding _TEMPLATE); (2) each entry's sha256 equals sha256(readFileSync(skills/<name>/SKILL.md)) — this hash is actively enforced at skill-load time (src/mcp/orchestration.ts's remote-fetch integrity check throws on mismatch). First run found 3 stale hashes (aws/gcp/azure-penetration-tester, edited after the manifest was last regenerated) and fixed them. Deliberately does NOT check description-field parity between the manifest and the SKILL.md frontmatter: verified empirically that all 91 differ by design — the frontmatter description carries Claude-facing trigger phrases, the manifest description is an independent short capability summary for the MCP prompt listing. Treating that as a bug would be enforcing an invariant that was never actually promised.

claims.verbatim: an unsigned policy cannot relax severity_block below the HIGH/CRITICAL floor
claims.note: An attacker who can edit the unsigned .mcp/policies/security-policy.json could otherwise set severity_block:[] and force every verdict to PASS. Verified: a workspace with severity_block:[] (no SECURITY_POLICY_HMAC_KEY set) and a CRITICAL-triggering sample must still produce status FAIL.

claims.verbatim: a check whose entire evidence source is unavailable emits EVAL_UNAVAILABLE_<NAME> instead of silently reporting clean
claims.note: The general form of the evaluability guarantee added by the Track E fail-open sweep. Verified concretely via checkCveExploitation (dependencies.ts): forcing npm audit to fail (empty PATH -> ENOENT, no stdout) must produce EVAL_UNAVAILABLE_NPM_AUDIT, not a silently-clean gate PASS. The other 11 EVAL_UNAVAILABLE_* sites added in the same sweep (cloud-controls, scanners x5, nuclei, runtime x2, auth-deep, business-logic) follow the identical pattern and are covered by the coverage-rule-remediation-parity claim (every one has a real rule id and a real template) plus manual code review, but are not independently adversarially tested here — extending this test to each would require a network/tool-failure seam per site, deferred as a follow-up rather than blocking this pass.

claims.verbatim: SECURITY_STRICT=1 flipping every permissive default and throwing at startup if a required key is absent
claims.note: Verified by actually spawning a child process with SECURITY_STRICT=1 and no HMAC keys set and asserting it fails at import time with the expected error, not by asserting the code should do this. Also manually verified (not part of the automated test, since it requires spawning and killing a long-running stdio server): the MCP server additionally requires SECURITY_MCP_SHARED_SECRET via assertStrictMcpAuthRequirements(), and with all three keys set, strict mode logs its startup banner and proceeds normally.

claims.verbatim: a control is marked satisfied only when a gate run completed its required steps with no adverse finding, never by default
claims.note: Already covered by the existing e2e test suite (added in the Wave 1 hardening pass): security.generate_compliance_report with no gate run must return 0 satisfied / all unverified, carry the not-an-audit caveat, and reject GDPR. Delegated rather than reimplemented — verify-claims.mjs runs `node --test dist/tests/legacy.test.js` once and this claim passes iff that run's exit code is 0.

claims.verbatim: This is what makes the "90% fixing, 10% advisory" operating mandate a deterministic property of the gate engine, verifiable by calling security.generate_remediations, rather than something that depends on the live agent's judgment call in the moment.

rewrite.newVerbatim: operating mandate achievable in practice: every detection ID has a concrete template to work from
rewrite.reason: The original claim overstated what the engine verifies. Every remediation template is a static {pattern, fix, explanation, references} object — nothing in src/ applies it; the calling agent reads the template and writes the fix by hand, and "verification" re-runs the same regex that originally fired, which cannot distinguish a real fix from a regex-evasion. The only path that is genuinely deterministic end-to-end is Terraform via security-mcp autoharden (apply -> re-detect -> revert). Rewritten 2026-07-17 to claim what's true: template coverage, not deterministic verification, except where autoharden actually delivers it.

claims.verbatim: This is what keeps the product's stated operating mandate, roughly 90% of findings resolved with a concrete fix and 10% left as advisory guidance, actually true, and turns it into a property the engine itself can verify rather than something the live agent merely tends toward

rewrite.newVerbatim: every finding the gate can raise now has a concrete template to work from, so the "90% fixing, 10% advisory" mandate is no longer bottlenecked by missing templates. Applying a template is still the calling agent's responsibility
rewrite.reason: Same overstatement as scoped-wiki-90pct-fixing-determinism, in ARCHITECTURE.md's parallel passage. Rewritten 2026-07-17.

claims.verbatim: so the audit trail cannot be silently rewritten after the fact

rewrite.newVerbatim: a rewrite requires the key, not just filesystem access
rewrite.reason: The original claim was unconditional. In the default (unsigned) configuration, the hash chain alone provides no forgery resistance to an attacker with filesystem write access to .mcp/agent-runs/ — they can simply recompute every hash over their edited content. Only the HMAC-signed case (SECURITY_AUDIT_HMAC_KEY configured) actually delivers tamper-evidence against that threat model, matching the residual-risk note already present elsewhere in the docs. Rewritten 2026-07-17 to scope the claim to the case where it holds.
